claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC dendritic alloy.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
Baseline TiVNbTa sustains approximately 40% strain at room temperature.
At approximately 1273 K, baseline TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa and a compressive strength of about 423 MPa.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 2–5 at% Cr to TiVNbTa.
Adding 2–5 at% Cr will produce finely dispersed nanoscale Cr-rich intermetallic precipitates in the BCC matrix.
The proposed Cr-rich precipitates will be coherent with the BCC matrix and thermally stable near 1273 K.
Cr addition will promote controlled precipitation during heat treatment or in-service exposure.
The Cr-rich precipitates will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
The Cr-rich precipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Precipitation strengthening will increase the high-temperature yield strength of TiVNbTa by approximately 30–50% relative to the baseline.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain useful elevated-temperature ductility.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain thermal conductivity suitable for efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
Preserving the overall BCC matrix structure will preserve high thermal conductivity.
Keeping Cr at approximately 2–5 at% will avoid excessive formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
Excessive brittle intermetallic formation would reduce ductility or thermal transport.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can possess favorable mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Alloying changes can substantially increase high-temperature hardness and yield strength in refractory HEAs.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 30–50% yield-strength increase, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant increase of at least 10%. An outcome between 10% and 30% would contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
